goal: The AI connection (key and month's cost) is read only by code about to call a model; screens ask a keyless 60-second memo; the month's AI cost is daily rows plus today; search reads no connection on a cache hit and has a ceiling on a miss; and a store's AI settings refresh that store's tag only.
why: Today commerce.ai_providers is read 12.4 times for each AI call made, the month's cost statement takes 37 to 57 ms a call, 319 prerendered entries carry the platform-wide tag 'ai-providers' that any owner's save expires, and a visitor's search can reach a model with no ceiling. After: at most 2 reads per call, under 5 ms, 0 entries with the wide tag, and a search_ai budget.

commits.title: The month's AI cost is the measured days plus today

changes.how: Export dayBounds (line 18) as it is.

In liveValue(), case 'ai_cost_micros' (lines 138 to 144), keep the 60 s memo and replace `first(aiCostSql(month, now, storeId))` by: one typedRow() read (z.object({ measured: col.minor, latest: nullable date text })) of `select coalesce(sum(value), 0)::bigint as measured, max(day)::text as latest from commerce.store_usage_daily where store_id = $1 and metric = 'ai_cost_micros' and day >= <the month's first day>::date`; then `const from = latest ? dayBounds(latest).to : month;` and the live part `first(aiCostSql(from, now, storeId))`; value = measured + live. A call is counted once: never in a measured day and in the live part. Note the trap and handle it: measureDay() writes NO row for a store that used nothing that day, so `latest` is the latest day WITH a row; the live part then starts after it and covers every later day, which is right but may span several days. That is still far less than the month. Do the same for 'marketing_emails' (emailsSql). Read through typedRow() with col helpers (money-reads.scan.test.ts).

Add two cases to the AI limit's describe: (a) a month of seeded commerce.ai_usage rows (source 'platform', with a price in force) on three past days of this month and today; run measureDay() for the three past days; expect usageNow(storeId, 'ai_cost_month_micros') (after forgetLimitMemos()) to equal the figure the old whole-month aiCostSql(month, now, storeId) gives, computed in the test; (b) the same with yesterday NOT measured: still equal. Then the existing 'is no AI for the month at the limit' case must pass unchanged.

Where a model price is saved (find the writer: rg -n 'insert into commerce.ai_prices|ai_model_prices' src/server), after a price whose start date is in the past is saved, call measureDay(day, false) for each day from max(that start date, the month's first day) to yesterday, so measured days are priced again. Add an int case for it beside the file's other tests. If no such writer file exists under that name, find it with the rg and apply the same there.

commits.title: A search answered from the cache reads no AI connection, and a miss is under a ceiling

changes.how: This commit needs a strong model. In searchProducts() (line 333) replace `const ai = await aiFor(shop.storeId, { feature: "search" });` by `const ai = await aiAbilities(shop.storeId);` and read `ai.textModel`, `ai.space` and `ai.minSimilarity` from it (same names). searchProducts() then sends no statement to commerce.ai_providers while the memo is warm; understandQuery() and queryVector() still call aiFor() inside their cache-miss callbacks, where a model is about to be called. Add an optional last parameter `visitor: string | null = null` to searchProducts() and pass it through to `understand(…)` and `vectorFor(…)` as a new last argument (extend the Understand and VectorFor types).

Add to BUDGETS, with comments in the file's style: `search_ai: { window: "minute", visitor: 20, store: 600 }` (a model call for a search nobody made before: a shopper types a few new searches a minute) and `search_ai_hour: { window: "hour", visitor: 300, store: 3000 }`. Do NOT add them to FAIL_CLOSED: past the budget, or when the count fails, the search runs by keyword and is never refused.

understandQuery() takes a new last parameter `visitor: string | null = null`. Inside the `cached(…, async () => { … })` callback (the cache-miss path, line 81), before aiFor(): `if (!(await searchAiRoom(storeId, visitor))) throw new AiError("Search is over its AI budget.");` (searchProducts() already catches a failed understanding and goes on by keyword: `.catch(skipped(…))`; a thrown error is not kept in the cache). Do the same in src/server/query-vector.ts queryVector() (new last parameter `visitor`, the same check first in its callback) but only when `feature === "search"` (recommendations have their own cap). Put `searchAiRoom(storeId, visitor)` in a new src/server/search-budget.ts: it returns true only if `takeBudget(storeId, "search_ai", visitor ?? "anon")` and `takeBudget(storeId, "search_ai_hour", visitor ?? "anon")` both allow, and the store's search tokens this month are under `SEARCH_AI_MONTHLY_TOKEN_CAP = 1_000_000` (a constant in src/lib/search.ts; the read is `select coalesce(sum(input_tokens + output_tokens), 0)::bigint from commerce.ai_usage where store_id = $1 and feature = 'search' and created_at >= date_trunc('month', now())`, through typedRow(), remembered 60 s per store with remembered()). A store on its own key is under the same ceiling. Whether owners get a setting for the cap, as recommendations have (recommendation_settings.monthly_token_cap), is a later choice: say so in the decision.

Line 92: pass the visitor to searchProducts(): `budgetVisitor(await headers())` (src/server/request-budget.ts; the section already renders per request). In src/server/chat-agent.ts line 272 pass the chat's own visitor key (the turn already has one for takeChatTurn(); read the function for its name) so the search page and the chat's search tool share the budget.

Seed a store with a platform AI provider whose calls are stubbed (as src/server/search.int.test.ts stubs them; read it first). Case 1: one visitor sends 200 different searches within a minute through searchProducts() with understandQuery and queryVector; count the stub's calls: at most 20 understandings and at most 20 vectors; every one of the 200 searches returns a result object (none throws). Case 2: the same search twice: wrap db() with a counting Proxy (see the pattern in src/server/assistant-notices-count.int.test.ts if step 0.17 is in; otherwise vi.mock('@/db/client') with a Proxy that counts statements whose text contains 'ai_providers') and expect 0 statements naming commerce.ai_providers during the second search. Case 3: with the month's search tokens seeded above the cap, a new search makes no model call and still returns keyword results.

changes.how: This commit needs a strong model. The test holds a table `PUBLIC_MODEL_PATHS: Record<entry file, ceiling>` of every route handler, page and server action under src/app that is outside 'src/app/admin' and 'src/app/api/cron' and can reach a model call, each with the name of what bounds it (a BUDGETS endpoint, takeChatTurn(), the recommendations' monthly cap, searchAiRoom()). Find the entries by walking static imports (the walker of src/lib/storefront-bundle.scan.test.ts, following server files) from each such entry to any module that calls completeText(, chatWithTools(, streamWithTools(, embedTexts( or the picture functions of src/server/ai.ts; the review counted nine. The test fails when the walk finds an entry that is not in the table, and when a table entry's ceiling name does not appear in the text of a file on its path. Under the AI usage rule (the one that says connections come from `aiFor(storeId, { feature, accountId })`) add: a screen that only shows or hides an AI button asks `aiAbilities()` (60 s, no key); a path a visitor can reach calls a model only under a ceiling listed in `public-model-paths.scan.test.ts`; search's is `searchAiRoom()`. Add one line to docs/capacity.md after its line on the AI limit memo (about line 612): the month's AI cost is the measured days plus a live part that starts after the latest measured day, and aiAbilities() is kept 60 seconds.

Append one row with the next free D-number (pull main first; `rg -o '^\| D[0-9]+' docs/decisions.md | tr -dc '0-9\n' | sort -n | tail -1`, plus 1). It records the five commits: aiTag(storeId) and the writers refreshing it; aiAbilities(); the month's cost from daily rows plus today (and re-measuring when a past price is saved); the search_ai budgets (20 a minute and 300 an hour a visitor, 600 and 3,000 a store) and the constant monthly cap of 1,000,000 tokens, taken only on a cache miss, never refusing a search; the scan of public model paths. Left for steps 0.27 and 0.28: jobs that read the connection per site before finding work. Platform: aiFor(null) and aiAbilities(null) keep the platform branch, and the platform's own AI settings refresh aiTag(null) only. No migration.

do_not: Do not cache the connection itself or keep a key in memory beyond a call: aiAbilities() holds flags, two model names and a number only.
Do not replace aiFor() where the code is about to call a model (turns, writers, jobs with work found).
Do not refuse a search that is over its budget: it runs by keyword.
Do not add search_ai to FAIL_CLOSED.
Do not make the abilities memo longer than 60 seconds.
Do not change a prompt or a tool's description (that would need a new eval recording).
Do not remove the 60 s memo of the AI cost in limits.ts.
Do not add a paid service for metering or limits.
stop_if: After commit one the build still has .meta files with 'ai-providers': report which and the cached function that tags them.
A caller named in commit two uses the connection for more than a yes or no.
The new month's cost differs from the whole-month sum in either new case: report both figures; do not loosen the assertion.
The existing case 'is no AI for the month at the limit, and only for that store' fails.
searchProducts()'s callers or types cannot carry the visitor without changing search results.
The public-paths walk finds more than about 15 or fewer than 5 entries (nine were counted): report the list before writing the table.
executor_why: Commit one is mechanical, but the cost boundary touches money and limits, and the search ceiling and the scan of public model paths need design judgement (who the visitor is on each path, what counts as a ceiling) that the brief cannot remove.
checked_in_code: I opened ai.ts (aiFor reads commerce.ai_providers with select * on every call; AI_TAG is 'ai-providers' at line 242), chat-agent.ts line 138, both AI actions files, limits.ts (the whole-month sum behind a 60 s memo), usage-meter.ts (dayBounds is not exported; a store with no use gets no daily row), search.ts (searchProducts calls aiFor before anything is looked up in the cache), query-understanding.ts, query-vector.ts and request-budget.ts. Corrections: CA-11 named the tag 'ai-providers:{id}', which would fail the done-when's grep for 0, so the brief uses SD-16's `ai:{id}`; there is no per-store search settings table (commerce.search_settings is the web search key), so the monthly cap is a constant, not a column, and no migration is needed; BUDGETS has one window per entry, so 'a minute per visitor and an hour per store' is two entries. The step's 'a job reads the connection once per run' is left to steps 0.27 and 0.28, which rework those jobs.
